title: Tenable One Unifies Exposure Management with Identity Security Data
summary: Tenable One now ingests identity security findings from third-party tools like Semperis Lightning, allowing you to manage identity risk in one unified platform.
body_markdown:
Tenable One now ingests identity findings from third-party sources, allowing you to assess and prioritize exposures related to stale and overprivileged accounts alongside your other security data, such as vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.


## **Key takeaways**


1. Managing identity risk should be an essential part of any exposure management program. However, in many organizations, exposure management programs often don’t include their identity-security teams.
2. Relying on siloed identity-security teams and tools leaves organizations vulnerable to attackers who chain identity flaws with other infrastructure vulnerabilities.
3. Tenable One now ingests findings from third-party identity security providers, so that you can prioritize such findings alongside all other types of exposures in your attack surface.


If your exposure management program can’t see identity risk, it’s missing a key piece of puzzle. According to SANS Institute’s “[2026 State of Identity Threats & Defenses Survey Insights Event](https://www.sans.org/research/identity-threat-detection-response-report) ” report, 55% of organizations suffered at least one identity-related breach during the 12-month survey period, and among those organizations, 21% suffered more than one breach.


Attackers often chain identity flaws with other security issues, such as vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, to create attack paths to your most critical systems and data. However, in many security programs,[identity security](https://www.tenable.com/cybersecurity-guide/learn/identity-access-management-iam) is siloed and managed by a separate team with its own tools.


This is a significant problem. Identity risk simply can’t be managed in isolation. It belongs in your[exposure management](https://www.tenable.com/cybersecurity-guide/learn/what-is-exposure-management) program, so that you can address identity exposures alongside other exposures in your on-premises infrastructure, cloud workloads, IoT devices, operational technology (OT) systems, and AI tools.


Many organizations have already invested in identity security tools they trust, and they shouldn’t have to replace those tools in order to manage identity findings in the[Tenable One Exposure Management Platform](https://www.tenable.com/products/tenable-one) . The[Tenable One Identity Exposure](https://www.tenable.com/products/identity-exposure) domain in Tenable One is designed to solve this problem by bringing in relevant data from third-party identity tools.


## **Two new ways to bring identity security data into Tenable One**


Tenable One now supports two new methods to ingest third-party identity data: first, a dedicated connector for Semperis Lightning; and second, custom ingestion of identity findings through the[Tenable One Open Connector](https://www.tenable.com/blog/new-tenable-one-open-connector-extends-third-party-integrations-unified-risk-visibility) . Alongside[Tenable One Identity Exposure](https://www.tenable.com/products/identity-exposure) , customers now have more choices in how they discover and manage identity risk within their exposure management program.


These two new ways to bring identity security data into Tenable One give your security team one picture of your organization’s cyber risk. Identity misconfigurations, stale accounts, and excessive privilege come into Tenable One as exposures to prioritize alongside your other security issues such as[vulnerabilities](https://www.tenable.com/principles/vulnerability-management-principles) and[cloud misconfigurations](https://www.tenable.com/cybersecurity-guide/learn/cloud-misconfigurations) , as part of the Tenable One dashboards and reports your team already uses.


Having identity security findings in one place reduces the chance that they’ll get overlooked. Stale and overprivileged accounts pile up quietly, and cleaning them up has usually meant logging in to your identity tool, exporting a list, and reviewing it. Now your team can weigh them against all your other security issues when deciding what to fix next, and focus on the riskiest accounts before an attacker finds them.


## **Bring Active Directory and Entra ID data from Semperis using the Tenable connector**


Our first dedicated identity connector is for[Semperis Lightning](https://www.semperis.com/lightning/) , which is designed to continuously monitor[Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID](https://www.tenable.com/blog/secure-ai-agent-identities-microsoft-entra-agent-id-tenable-one) for identity misconfigurations, privilege abuse, stale accounts, and authentication weaknesses. The connector brings accounts, groups and roles as assets in Tenable One.


Take a stale service account with a tier 0 privilege, the most privileged tier in Microsoft’s enterprise access model. Semperis flags it as an indicator of exposure (IoE), with a severity rating, a description, and remediation guidance. The connector brings that IoE into Tenable One as a finding on the account itself, with its severity rating and the steps to remediate. Tenable One logs the account’s privileged designation as a tag, so your team can see it at a glance.


The connector also keeps Tenable One and Semperis Lightning automatically in sync. When your team fixes the problem and the IoE passes its next Semperis check, the finding moves to the Fixed queue in Tenable One.


You also control what identity security data gets imported into Tenable One. You can choose to ingest data from Active Directory, Entra ID, or both, and you can filter out findings by picking a minimum severity level.


How to Bring Semperis Identity Data into Tenable One, Identify Crown Jewel Accounts, and Act on Findings. The demo covers connecting Semperis to Tenable One, locating key assets, and moving from findings to remediation. Connecting the data source: In Connectors, add a new connector and filter by the Identity Security category. Configure the Semperis connector to ingest identity security data directly into Tenable One. For other identity providers, the Tenable One Open Connector is designed to bring security data from custom sources into the platform, including another identity security tool, a homegrown system, or a spreadsheet. Analyzing assets: In Assets, filter the view by Semperis to isolate identity security data. The view shows 11.3k assets imported from Semperis, including 44 new assets in the last 7 days. Accounts are the asset type attackers typically target first, so open the Accounts asset type and add a filter for crown jewel accounts. The resulting list of crown jewel account assets is sorted by number of active findings. Investigating findings: Open an account with 14 active findings, including several critical findings. The account page shows full details, including account type and relevant tags. The findings list for the account is ranked by severity. Open an individual finding to see the details needed to understand the issue and decide how to fix it. Remediation: Use Tenable Hexa AI for remediation. With a simple prompt it can create separate JIRA tickets for each critical finding, including all relevant details. Complete the action and send the ticket to move from finding to fix and close the gap.


## **Ingest identity data from other sources with the Tenable One Open Connector**


[Tenable One Open Connector](https://www.tenable.com/blog/new-tenable-one-open-connector-extends-third-party-integrations-unified-risk-visibility) brings security data from custom sources into the platform, and now it accepts identity data too, whether it lives in another identity security tool, a homegrown system, or a spreadsheet.


Open Connector also handles the mechanics. Connect to your cloud or storage database of choice and Tenable One picks up new files automatically as they refresh. Prefer to do it by hand? Upload CSV, Excel, or ZIP files directly. You decide how your identity security tools fields map to Tenable One’s, including combining them or keeping them separate. Tenable One then deduplicates and normalizes the data, so an account reported by two sources shows up as one finding.


## **Also new: More connectors for application security, and asset inventory tools**


Identity is the newest category we have added to Tenable One Open Connector, which currently features more than 400 validated integrations. However, it’s not the only area in which we’re adding connectors. We’ve shipped nine new Tenable One Connectors for application security and endpoint tools.


- **Application security:**[GitHub Code Scanning](https://docs.tenable.com/exposure-management/Content/connectors/github-code-scanning-connector.htm) ,[GitHub Dependabot](https://docs.tenable.com/exposure-management/Content/connectors/github-dependabot-connector.htm) ,[GitLab](https://docs.tenable.com/exposure-management/Content/connectors/gitlab-connector.htm) ,[Veracode SAST](https://docs.tenable.com/exposure-management/Content/connectors/veracode-sast-connector.htm) ,[Veracode SCA](https://docs.tenable.com/exposure-management/Content/connectors/veracode-sca-connector.htm) ,[Invicti](https://docs.tenable.com/exposure-management/Content/connectors/invicti-connector.htm) , and[Checkmarx](https://docs.tenable.com/exposure-management/Content/connectors/checkmarx-one-connector.htm)
- **Asset inventory:**[ChromeOS](https://docs.tenable.com/exposure-management/Content/connectors/chrome-os-connector.htm) ,[Asimily](https://docs.tenable.com/exposure-management/Content/connectors/asimily-connector.htm)
